correctness.rationale: With unit proximal step, two strict scalar contractions x/(kappa+1) and (x+1)/2 (kappa>=1) admit a unique invariant law for each p in [0,1] and all finite starts. Independent stationarity gives mean mu=(1-p)w2/W and variance p(1-p)w1^2w2^2/(W^2 S), with w1=kappa/(kappa+1),w2=1/2,W=pw1+(1-p)w2,S=p(2w1-w1^2)+(1-p)(2w2-w2^2)>0. Fixed equal-weight target x*=1/(kappa+1): R=Var+(mu-x*)^2. Independently differentiated exact rational R to recover derivative sign P(p)=A p^2+B p-3(kappa+1)^4 where A=(kappa-1)(kappa+3)(kappa^2+4kappa+5), B=6(kappa+1)^2(kappa+3). P increases on [0,1], P(0)<0 and P(1)=-2kappa(kappa+2)(kappa^2-2kappa-7); hence unique optimizer interior for 1<=kappa<1+2sqrt(2), exactly p=1 for kappa>= boundary (root p=1 at equality). The unbiased-stationary-mean p_ub=(kappa+1)/(kappa+3) is less than optimal for kappa>1 and gives R(p_ub)/R(1)=kappa^2/(2kappa+1). Source derivative, rational boundary, unbiased identities were independently reconstructed with SymPy. Fixed objective is NOT optimized in the usual unbiased algorithm sense by p=1.
residual_risks: At p=1 the algorithm always selects only f1 and retains nonzero fixed-objective error for finite kappa; the claim is solely terminal stationary square risk.

value.rationale: The stationary variance/bias policy problem is a natural quantitative diagnostic of constant-step stochastic resolvents. Its exact critical curvature 1+2sqrt(2), unique optimal policy, and unbounded relative risk of an unbiased stationary mean reveal a non-obvious phase boundary with an explicit warning about implicit objective shift. It is a motivated small theoretical benchmark rather than a universal recommendation to omit components.
